correctness.rationale: For each N=1,..,4, independent rate-one walkers give a transient 4-state-per-walker generator; the occupancy-count lumped generator has C(N+3,3) states and diagonal -N. Its exact linear solutions (-Q)u=1 and (-Q)v=u give first moment u and half second moment v. A complete standard-library Fraction checker recalculates the claimed signs and separately uses the 4^N labeled generator for N<=3. The renewal differentiation then establishes strictly opposite local reset effects and matrix-continuity gives robustness. No numerical extrapolation or all-N claim.

originality.rationale: The one-team renewal identity is known (Biroli et al., Section IV, Equations 20-29). The asserted result is instead an exact rational sign reversal for a concrete five-state killed chain: negative at N=1,2,3, positive at N=4, with an open robustness argument. The inspected Biroli study uses Brownian motion on an unbounded line and its reported numerical team threshold is different. No explicit or logically dominating finite path result was identified in the recorded source comparisons. Known general moment criteria could make the calculation derivative of prior methods; this residual priority risk is acknowledged.

value.rationale: A finite five-vertex network displays an exact team-size-dependent sign reversal under common restarting between three and four identical searchers. This gives a reproducible tiny testbed for collective reset policies distinct from the known Brownian half-line threshold, with a mathematically meaningful choice of a reset rate near zero and robust behavior under small rate perturbations. It is a narrow but natural structural boundary rather than an arbitrary graph table.
